entries.heading: CHEM 117. Biomedical Research in Health Disparities (4)
entries.name: Biomedical Research in Health Disparities
entries.description: Surveys historical research harms, race and health outcomes alongside genomic and biological explanations of disparities and emerging biomedical interventions.
notes: The prerequisite is an alternative: CHEM 40B, 40CH, or 41C. The earlier pool’s comma-only list is not treated as requiring all three courses.

Listed title: Biomedical Research and Health Disparities. Current title: Biomedical Research in Health Disparities. The change is the in/and preposition in the same biomedical-disparities subject or the explicit III sequence number for 6C/6CH; current content aligns without asserting a different course identity.

category_review.locator: CHEM 117. Biomedical Research in Health Disparities (4)
category_review.rationale: Historical harms and race-related disparities are explicit social inquiry, while genomics, biological mechanisms and personalized medicine form a distinct biomedical component. The description does not establish one as dominant.

entries.heading: CHEM 11. The Periodic Table (4)
entries.name: The Periodic Table
entries.description: Introduces atoms and small inorganic molecules as the basis of the material world.
notes: Intended for nonscience majors; this is not stated as an exclusive major restriction. Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 4 and CHEM 11.
No formal Prerequisites clause is printed in this current block. Null records that omission, not absence of preparation or enrollment conditions.

category_review.rationale: Atomic and molecular chemistry is substantive domain science, independent of the nonscience-major audience.

entries.heading: CHEM 4. Chemical Thinking (4)
entries.name: Chemical Thinking
entries.description: Develops models of matter and structure-property relationships to explain and predict chemical behavior in preparation for general chemistry.
notes: Enrollment is restricted to first-year and sophomore students. Concurrent MATH 3C, 4C, or 10A or higher is recommended, not required by this block.
One-quarter preparation for general chemistry. Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 4 and CHEM 11; this exclusion does not establish course identity.
No formal Prerequisites clause is printed in this current block. Null records that omission, not absence of preparation or enrollment conditions.

category_review.rationale: Chemical models and material behavior define domain science; introductory preparation is not computer-science foundations.

entries.heading: CHEM 6C. General Chemistry III (4)
entries.name: General Chemistry III
entries.description: Continues general chemistry with reaction kinetics, acid-base equilibrium, electrochemistry, coordination compounds and introductory nuclear chemistry.
notes: Third quarter of a three-quarter sequence intended for science and engineering majors; this is an intended audience, not an exclusive major restriction.
CHEM 6C cannot be taken for credit after CHEM 6CH. The reverse order is explicitly allowed by the 6CH block, so the restriction is directional.

Listed title: General Chemistry. Current title: General Chemistry III. The change is the in/and preposition in the same biomedical-disparities subject or the explicit III sequence number for 6C/6CH; current content aligns without asserting a different course identity.

category_review.rationale: The explicit content consists of chemical mechanisms and principles.

entries.heading: CHEM 6CH. Honors General Chemistry III (4)
entries.name: Honors General Chemistry III
entries.description: Studies the third-quarter general-chemistry topics at an accelerated honors level, including kinetics, equilibria and electrochemical, coordination and nuclear chemistry.
notes: Third quarter of a three-quarter honors sequence intended for well-prepared science and engineering majors, not an exclusive major restriction.
May receive credit for CHEM 6CH after CHEM 6C, but may not subsequently take CHEM 6C for credit. Both CHEM 6BH and MATH 20B are required.

Listed title: Honors General Chemistry. Current title: Honors General Chemistry III. The change is the in/and preposition in the same biomedical-disparities subject or the explicit III sequence number for 6C/6CH; current content aligns without asserting a different course identity.

category_review.rationale: The source explicitly refers to CHEM 6C content at a higher level and faster pace; that separately guarded block identifies chemical subject matter.

notes: No exact CHEM 15 heading appears in the reviewed 2026–27 Chemistry and Biochemistry chapter. No substitute, cancellation or university-wide absence is inferred.

entries.heading: CHEM 171. Environmental Chemistry I (4)
entries.name: Environmental Chemistry I
entries.description: Introduces environmental chemistry through atmospheric pollution, ozone, climate, radioactive waste, resource use and energy choices.
notes: Only one of CHEM 149A and CHEM 171 may receive credit. This exclusion alone does not establish an alias.

category_review.rationale: The description frames environmental issues through chemical concerns and atmospheric science. Risks and benefits do not by themselves establish coequal political or ethical analysis.

entries.heading: CHEM 172. Environmental Chemistry II (4)
entries.name: Environmental Chemistry II
entries.description: Examines chemical cycles in solids and liquids across time, including disruptions from society, volcanism and extinction and examples beyond Earth.
notes: CHEM 171 is recommended preparation. CHEM 6C or 6CH is the actual prerequisite; the recommendation is not promoted into a required sequence.

category_review.rationale: Environmental chemical processes and elemental cycles are primary; societal perturbations are studied within that physical framework.

entries.heading: CHEM 173. Atmospheric Chemistry (4)
entries.name: Atmospheric Chemistry
entries.description: Applies chemistry to atmospheric composition, reactions, aerosols and geochemical cycles associated with ozone, acid rain and climate.
notes: May be coscheduled with CHEM 273; this does not establish course identity or impose graduate eligibility.

category_review.rationale: Atmospheric chemical mechanisms are substantive scientific domain knowledge.

entries.listed_name: Origins of Life and the Universe
entries.heading: CHEM 111. Origins of Life and the Universe (4)
entries.name: Origins of Life and the Universe
entries.description: Traces chemical evolution from stars and planets to Earth’s atmosphere, oceans and early life, including searches for chemical evidence of life elsewhere.

category_review.locator: CHEM 111. Origins of Life and the Universe (4)
category_review.rationale: Biogeochemical evolution and chemical detection techniques are scientific content, not historical-cultural interpretation despite a long time scale.

entries.heading: CHEM 145. Biofuels and Renewable Materials (4)
entries.name: Biofuels and Renewable Materials
entries.description: Studies the chemistry, biochemical pathways, processing and analysis used to produce biofuels and renewable materials.

category_review.rationale: Chemical and biochemical production technologies and analytical practice are the explicit applied domain.

entries.heading: CHEM 151. Molecules that Changed the World (4)
entries.name: Molecules that Changed the World
entries.description: Explores notable natural molecules and how discovery, synthesis, modification and use of molecules affect society.

category_review.locator: CHEM 151. Molecules that Changed the World (4)
category_review.rationale: Molecular discovery and chemical synthesis organize the description. Societal effects provide context without a separately stated social-analysis method or objective.

entries.heading: CHEM 174. Chemical Principles of Marine Systems (4)
entries.name: Chemical Principles of Marine Systems
entries.description: Explains the distribution and aqueous behavior of seawater elements through atomic structure, bonding and periodic chemical properties.
notes: The current description explicitly cross-lists SIO 141 and disallows credit for both SIO 141 and CHEM 174. The reviewed current SIO chapter has no exact SIO 141 heading; this one-sided current evidence is retained for primary identity/version review, with no identity group emitted.

category_review.locator: CHEM 174. Chemical Principles of Marine Systems (4)
category_review.rationale: Marine chemical mechanisms establish a domain-science subject.

entries.heading: CHEM 143C. Organic Chemistry Laboratory (4)
entries.name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
entries.description: Identifies unknown organic compounds using chemical and physical laboratory techniques.
notes: Enrollment is limited to Chemistry and Biochemistry department majors unless space is available; students outside those majors are not absolutely prohibited. Program or materials fees may apply.

The printed prerequisite clause contains alternative laboratory courses and alternative lecture courses joined by and. Its compressed numbering and AND/OR wording are preserved without an unsupported Boolean expansion.

category_review.rationale: Organic-compound identification is concrete laboratory practice.
